reason: The 70% LTV falls within the Fannie Mae conventional term sheet's stated maximum of 80% LTV, and a 40-unit existing stabilized property satisfies the five-unit-minimum, existing-stabilized property type described in the source. However, the term sheet also states a minimum DSCR of 1.25x, and debt service was not supplied, so DSCR cannot be computed or verified. With one of the two disclosed core financial thresholds untested, the deal cannot be called 'financially qualified' — only that the LTV metric sits inside the disclosed range while remaining criteria are unverified. The source further notes that the guidelines do not establish approval of a specific borrower, so no approval conclusion is supportable. Stabilized status also remains unconfirmed against the typical 90% occupancy for 90 days benchmark (a typical guideline that the source says permits case-by-case consideration for pre-stabilized deals, not an absolute test). The Freddie Mac Conventional Small announcement is not applicable to a Fannie Mae term-sheet fit question and does not state a complete set of underwriting criteria.
missing_information: Annual debt service (rate, amortization, term) needed to compute DSCR against the 1.25x minimum
Underwritten net operating income / net cash flow
Requested loan amount and appraised value supporting the stated 70% LTV
Occupancy history to confirm stabilized status (typical 90% for 90 days)
Whether nonrecourse execution is sought and whether loan exceeds the $750,000 threshold with standard carve-outs
Borrower/sponsor credit, experience, and net worth/liquidity information
Publication or effective date of the Fannie Mae term sheet (listed as null) to confirm currency of the stated LTV and DSCR parameters
Any lender-issued commitment, quote, or approval document
